Open-data attribution for cameras, roads and the basemap
Light by day, dark by night — follows sunrise and sunset at your location.

How readouts with a decimal — distances, g, fuel economy, mount offset, map zoom — are written. Speeds round to whole km/h, so they never show one either way. Map coordinates always use a point, so a latitude/longitude pair stays readable.
Start a trip automatically when driving is detected
Detour\'s tracker stays on, with its notification showing, even when you\'re parked. It needs physical activity access to tell that you\'ve stopped, so it can switch itself off until you ride again.

Detour\'s tracker stays on, with its notification showing, even when you\'re parked. Set location access to \"Allow all the time\" and it can switch itself off while parked, then wake when you ride away.
Turn instructions read aloud while navigating, here and on the car screen. Mutable mid-drive from the speaker button there.
Go currently launches: %1$s. Long-press Go to change it.
In-app navigation skips motorways (car mode; moto never uses them)
Prefer real roads over narrow rural lanes, service roads and unpaved tracks
Take a toll road, bridge or tunnel only when there is no reasonable way around
Cross water by road where a bridge or tunnel will do
Keep off gravel, dirt and sand, even on roads that are otherwise real roads
Your routing server can\'t do this yet
Drawn where you are, on the phone map and on the car screen. Vehicles turn to face the way you\'re heading.
The line drawn to your destination, on the phone map and on the car screen. While navigating, the part you have already driven fades to the darker shade.
Where the map sits while following you. It zooms out up to two levels at speed and back in near a turn.
When navigation starts, Detour downloads the map up to 5 km either side of the route (at most 150 MB), so it keeps drawing where the signal drops. Starting a new route replaces it.
Uncover the map together: your accepted friends see the roads you have driven, and you see theirs. Only friends who share back can see yours. Off, nobody sees either.
All fog-of-war progress will be permanently deleted. Saved trips are kept.
Broadcast turn-by-turn over Bluetooth Low Energy for a handlebar-mounted screen — turn, distance, speed, speed limit, road name, and remaining distance/ETA.

Relay title, artist, and playback position from whatever\'s playing (Spotify, etc.) to the handlebar display. Reads media sessions only, never notification content — Android requires notification access to do either, so the permission name is broader than what\'s actually used.
Enabled. Also turn on \"Broadcast to external display\" above — music shares that Bluetooth connection.

Add a Bluetooth device to a vehicle. When it\'s connected, trips log under that vehicle automatically. With nothing connected, a trip that never picks up real driving pace is dropped rather than saved.
Grant Bluetooth access to add your paired devices.
Trips stop logging as %1$s when this device connects. You can add it back from the paired list.
No unassigned paired devices. Pair the device in Android\'s Bluetooth settings first, or remove it from another vehicle.
Shown in your history and to your convoy. Leave blank to use the device name.
No rotation sensor on this phone

Corrects for a mount that isn\'t perfectly upright on the handlebar, so straight-line riding reads as 0° lean. Sit the bike upright on its wheels, engine off, phone in its normal mount, then calibrate.
Config imported — restart the app to use the new servers
It replaces the server addresses on this device with the file\'s. What is there now is not recoverable.
Optional: your own address for routing, search, sync and live.

Optional: one self-hosted address for routing, search, sync and the convoy live relay (see the one-hostname layout in one-hostname layout). Leave empty to use the built-in routing/search servers, with sync and live off.
Your server suggests a routing address: %1$s
Your server suggests a search address: %1$s
“%1$s” is not a server address — use http:// or https:// and a host name.

For a deployment split across hostnames. Anything left empty uses the server address above. Routing and search cannot share one host with sync, because the API answers /api/trips and the search server answers /api/ — so one address cannot serve both.
If your search server is unreachable, retry via the public Photon instance (komoot.io) — sends the query, your approximate location and the coordinates of places being named off your own hardware.
All five addresses are cleared and the app falls back to the built-in server.
All five addresses are cleared and the app falls back to the public servers.
Your trips, explored area and badges are kept on your own server.
Trips, explored area and badges are merged with your server after every trip and on app start, so a reinstall restores everything. Uses the Server URL under Server settings.
Not signed in — open Friends to create an account.
Keep your server setup in a file, and import it after a reinstall.
Save the server addresses to a file. After a reinstall, import it instead of typing them again.
The file does not carry your sign-in. After importing it on another phone, sign in there again.

Times the slow parts of the app against how much data they ran over, so it is possible to see whether they are getting slower as your history grows. Stays on this device — never synced, never backed up.
Export failed: the timings file could not be saved. Free up some storage and try again.
never probed, or no probe has answered

Pair a vehicle\'s OBD2 adapter (a Bluetooth ELM327 dongle plugged into the port) for accurate speed instead of GPS. Not a score to chase, not new history — just a more accurate speed reading while it\'s connected.
No other paired devices to use as an OBD2 adapter.
%1$s goes back to GPS speed until the adapter is paired again from this screen.
If the trip fuel figure reads high or low against your car\'s own display, nudge this.
Add a vehicle under Tracking & vehicles first.
Couldn\'t reach the adapter — check it\'s plugged in and Bluetooth is on.
The adapter didn\'t answer the handshake — a cheap clone may need a re-plug.
Connected, but the vehicle sent no data — try again with the ignition on.
Bluetooth connection error — moving out of range or the adapter reset.
